newsitem.title: UK: Cathay says UK-HK cargo full for 5-day handover.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says UK-HK cargo full for 5-day handover.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways said its UK-Hong Kong cargo capacity will be flying fully booked over the colony's five-day-long handover celebration period, starting Friday.
"Traditionally, this is a quiet airfreight month on the route, but not this year," the HK-based carrier's north UK cargo manager Ivor Llewellyn told Reuters.
"However, it is because of general buoyant economic conditions between Britain and Hong Kong that we are doing so well, not particularly anything to do with the handover," he said.
Britain will officially return the colony to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday, June 30.

Between Friday and Monday, Cathay is operating three ex-UK, 100-tonne capacity Boeing 747 freighter flights and 10 747 passenger services, which can each carry around 15 tonnes per flight, from a combination of London and Manchester.
"We are completely full with cargo on these. Although sterling has been strong for some time, this has not affected our ex-UK cargo business to Hong Kong," said Llewellyn.
He added that sister, all-cargo carrier Air Hong Kong (AHK), controlled 75 percent by Cathay, was also doing well with its six weekly Manchester-HK 747 freighter flights.
"So well in fact that we have asked them if they can fly some of our own equipment to Hong Kong -- including empty containers -- and have been told that they can't handle it," he said.
Llewellyn added that Cathay could not pinpoint why there was such an air cargo boom in UK-HK traffic during what is traditionally a slow season.
"There is no logic to it at all," he stated.
--- Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
